sec: Henderson–Hasselbalch and renal handling of excess HCO₃⁻ · p824

items.q: The Henderson–Hasselbalch equation is printed in which form for the bicarbonate pair?
items.exp: pH = pKa + log [HCO₃⁻](A⁻)/[H₂CO₃](HA) = pKa + log [HCO₃⁻]/PaCO₂, since H₂CO₃ is in equilibrium with dissolved CO₂. (Book p824)
[H⁺] = 24 × PaCO₂/HCO₃⁻ — the relation used throughout ABG interpretation. (Book p824)

items.q: Match the acid–base change to its respiratory consequence — 1) ↑HCO₃⁻/metabolic alkalosis  2) Respiratory response  3) Purpose of the change … A) To maintain H⁺ constant  B) Leads to ↑PaCO₂  C) Hypoventilation
items.exp: ↑HCO₃⁻/metabolic alkalosis leads to ↑PaCO₂ (labelled respiratory alkalosis on p824) to maintain H⁺ constant. (Book p824)

items.q: ‘Page 824 labels the ↑PaCO₂ response of metabolic alkalosis “respiratory alkalosis”, whereas the compensation table on p828 calls the same change “respiratory acidosis”.’
opts: True — the two pages print different labels for the same hypoventilation response
False — both pages label the response respiratory acidosis
False — both pages label the response respiratory alkalosis
False — p828 states that metabolic alkalosis has no respiratory compensation
items.exp: p824 prints ‘↑PaCO₂/respiratory alkalosis (to maintain H⁺ constant)’ while the p828 compensation table pairs metabolic alkalosis with a respiratory acidosis compensation — the same ↑PaCO₂ change under two labels. (Book p824)

items.q: A patient with persistent vomiting has a high bicarbonate. Which renal behaviour explains why the alkalosis persists?
opts: The kidney fails to excrete the excess HCO₃⁻
The kidney excretes the excess HCO₃⁻ and conserves Cl⁻
The kidney converts HCO₃⁻ to H₂CO₃ and excretes CO₂
The kidney reabsorbs Cl⁻ in exchange for HCO₃⁻ excretion
items.exp: Excess HCO₃⁻ handled by the kidney gives two outcomes: excreted with Cl⁻ conserved → no metabolic alkalosis; failure to excrete → metabolic alkalosis. (Book p824)

items.q: Match the renal handling of excess HCO₃⁻ — 1) HCO₃⁻ excreted  2) HCO₃⁻ not excreted  3) Organ deciding the outcome … A) Metabolic alkalosis  B) No metabolic alkalosis  C) Kidney
items.exp: If excess HCO₃⁻ is excreted and Cl⁻ conserved there is no metabolic alkalosis; failure to excrete produces metabolic alkalosis. (Book p824)

items.q: All but one of the following are printed in the excess-HCO₃⁻ flowchart. Which is the odd one out?
opts: Lungs are the sole route of HCO₃⁻ disposal
The kidney is the deciding organ for excess HCO₃⁻
Excretion of HCO₃⁻ occurs with conservation of Cl⁻
Failure to excrete HCO₃⁻ causes metabolic alkalosis
items.exp: The flowchart routes excess HCO₃⁻ through the kidney: excretion with Cl⁻ conservation → no alkalosis; failure to excrete → metabolic alkalosis. (Book p824)
